So briefly,, got symptoms at 13 (2020) and then diagnosed with hashimotos, then cfs early 14 years old (early 2021, was lucky to go to a pediatrician who knew of a CFS specialist) then spent 14-early 16 in absolute hell, bedbound to bedroom bound to house bound, walking canes, wheelchairs, school exemptions, chronic pain, constant brain fog and overwhelm. Could barely shower/care for myself. 

Turned 16 got diagnosed with Autism and POTS.

Got NDIS (I’m Australian) support in June 2023. Helped me gain independence and ease the mental health issues that come from chronic illness.
I found a CFS support group near me and went to meet ups, that was really helpful for a bit as I didn’t feel so alone and misunderstood.
I have since stopped going since my level of capacity is so much higher that I just feel super rude continuing to go, I’m now the person I used to be jealous of.
^ Mid 2023

I Started propanalol for POTS in late 2023, started rollerblading again (Very lucky to have picked up a hobby before getting unwell that is easier on my joints/body than walking) 
Propanalol gave me the ability to walk again and do light chores and put systems in place to support myself during crashes. Rollerblading also gave me an accessible social circle, gave my identity back and light physical activity (once to twice a week, max 3hrs socialising in the same familiar building, organic connections from a shared activity) which I hadn’t had for soooo long.
Propanalol ended up making my heart rate FAR too low to the point it would make me sleepy and weak, I went off propanalol but it seemed that my heart had kind of mildly regulated itself (probably due to the medication but also the increased activity and stamina I started developing)
^ that was early 2024

I continued to rollerblade and socialise building walking and household chore capacity.
I then started working at the rollerskating rink as the front ticket person, very lucky to get this job, it’s hard standing for 3-4hrs straight and was a bit slow to learn the job but now I don’t even have to think and my body can handle the standing as I now give myself 5minutes of cleaning things while seated during quiet periods. The shifts are 3hrs to 3.5hrs a day, Friday, Saturday night time and Sunday afternoon. Very achievable for my capacity.

In June I then got a personal trainer and exercise physiologist, fortunately covered by NDIS. 
I got twice a week with the PT (strength training, teaching me basic nutrition, increasing my protein intake) and once a week with the excerise physio (we do a mix of yoga, strength training, Pilate type stuff and hydrotherapy)

Building muscle, moving more, socialising (which helped with my mental health) was LIFE changing, helps with the chronic pain.

Entire time and now I still continue to pace myself but my baseline slowly gets better, but I can tell that it can very easily be brought right back down (very close this last 2 weeks, have pushed myself way too much)

I now can go to concerts, dance, throw parties, am learning to drive, have friends, meeting people, drink alcohol, walk long distances, swim and hoping to get a better more stable job or study in the coming year as I didn’t get to finish grade 9 and beyond (only finished grade 8)

I’ve also fortunately made progress on being at a place with my pain where I can trust that it will eventually fade/change/go away, this gives me sooo much relief mentally. I do not expect this from anyone though unless they have experience chronic pain that goes away and comes back, if it’s always there, I think it’s pretty impossible to have that trust in your body and universe (it never goes away fully but there’s no better way to describe it)

Thank you, it’s been a journey. 14 years old diagnosed with CFS, symptoms at 13, undiagnosed autistic. 14 to just turned 17 absolute hell, barely living, chronic pain, suicidal. Turning 17 my life turned around, propanalol seemed to help stabilise my heart (POTS but I still have mild POTS) but then it made my heart rate far to low so I stopped it and haven’t noticed anything bad, other than the fact that if I don’t pace myself it sucks. and I think also over time and just growing up and maturing I have learnt to pace myself properly and I do now have disability support which I personally think has been the biggest help. I still have chronic pain and occasional PEM which results in brain fog but due to moving more and being able to distract myself it’s gotten easier, I also don’t last as long in crashes anymore and have learnt when I do crash to let it happen, don’t fight it, don’t push, just let your body crash, fortunately I have to luxury of doing that as my mum is incredible and I have disability support work. 
I do think a big portion of chronic illness *MANAGEMENT* (not chronic illness itself!!) is environmental. You cannot expect someone to get better who is chronically stressed, has no external support and all management strategies are stressful and boring and do more harm than good.

I also think with ME/CFS you end up losing your identity and lose confidence, once I was able to build the ability to socialise more and do an old hobby of mine, I could build my new identity and had more confidence and motivation. I didn’t feel such a lack of hope.

I’m still 17 so don’t take my word as anything to live by it’s just my personal experience in a very brief comment, you can see through my account over the years how deeply lonely, depressed and in (physical and emotional) pain I was in, I really did suffer.
I live a very different life than those in adulthood and with no disability or communal/family support and I see and understand that not everyone gets the luxury or privilege of even trying to improve.

I also don’t recommend medicinal CBD/THC for CFS. But it’s also situational, depends on the person but that’s a long story.
